patch.value: Sentry PM-CLI-2W: rejected unknown-author acknowledgments are emitted as high production errors

The public unknown-author acknowledgment command correctly rejects a stale or non-actionable target, but the handled TypeError crosses the observability boundary as a high unresolved Sentry issue. This makes expected operator validation noise indistinguishable from a product failure and can block release health.

The observability boundary classifies this exact validation family as expected without masking unexpected errors; focused tests prove positive and negative classification; the Sentry release gate recognizes the outcome; PM-CLI-2W is dispositioned with live evidence.
Keep release health sensitive to genuine failures without penalizing expected validation paths.
Preserves a trustworthy Sentry signal and avoids false release blockers.
Reduces high-severity alert noise while retaining structured operator feedback.
The same invalid request remains rejected but no longer appears as an unresolved high production failure.
Live closeout found PM-CLI-2W as the only unresolved issue seen in the last 24 hours.
Run the unknown-author acknowledgment command against a stale or non-actionable event target such as pm-iimv:1; observe a handled CLI rejection and Sentry PM-CLI-2W.
Expected validation refusals remain structured CLI diagnostics and do not create high unresolved production issues; unexpected failures remain observable.
Sentry PM-CLI-2W recorded two handled TypeError events on 2026-08-06 from release pm-cli@2026.8.5.
Release operators see a high unresolved production error for a correctly rejected request; no data corruption occurred.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
Fixed 2026-08-07 at the observability boundary rather than in the waiver list, with the release gate covered as well.

Root cause. The five argument validations in the public acknowledgment primitive raised bare TypeErrors. A TypeError carries no exit code, so the CLI mapped it to the generic failure code, and the boundary reports any handled error whose exit code is not usage, not-found or conflict. A correct refusal of a stale target therefore crossed into the error channel as a high unresolved production issue and gated the 2026-08-07 scheduled cut.

Product fix. The five validations now refuse through one helper that raises a PmCliError at the usage exit code with a stable machine code: selector_conflict, required_values_missing, target_unreadable and target_not_actionable. The boundary already classifies usage as expected, so the family is excluded at the source rather than allowlisted after the fact, and every other failure inside the same primitive keeps its own exit code and remains reportable. Messages are unchanged.

Verified live on the exact invocation that produced the blocking issue. The same event coordinate that generated the Sentry error now exits 2 with a structured problem envelope carrying code history_author_acknowledge_target_unreadable, so the occurrence cannot recur through the supported surface.

Gate fix. The four acknowledgment refusal families are declared in the expected-handled patterns of the release gate, so they stay classified if expected-error capture is ever enabled for a release smoke, and the release contract spec asserts the declaration.

Tests. A focused spec asserts the positive classification, that each of the four families raises a PmCliError at the usage exit code carrying its declared code, and the negative control asserts that an unexpected failure inside the same primitive is still an Error that is not a PmCliError, so the reclassification cannot mask a genuine fault. Full suite green at 6904 tests.

Escape recorded. The gate that blocked the release matches production errors by message prose and reads none of the 236 codes the product declares; that consumer defect and the missing join between a closed item and the external issue whose window gates the cut are filed separately, because neither is repaired by this fix.
